questions.stem: Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C. Historically, sailors on long voyages often developed scurvy. Captain James Cook prevented scurvy by providing his crew with citrus fruits. What is the role of vitamin C in the body?

options.text: Vitamin C is needed for energy production in mitochondria
Vitamin C is needed for collagen production, which maintains healthy connective tissue, skin, and blood vessels
Vitamin C is needed to make haemoglobin
Vitamin C strengthens bones by adding calcium

questions.explanation: Vitamin C is essential for the synthesis of collagen, a structural protein found in connective tissue, skin, blood vessels, and gums. Without vitamin C, collagen cannot be properly formed, leading to symptoms of scurvy including bleeding gums, loose teeth, bruising, poor wound healing, and weakened blood vessels.

questions.stem: A child in a developing country has a swollen belly, thin limbs, and flaky skin. They have been eating mostly maize (corn) porridge. Which deficiency disease is most likely, and what nutrient is lacking?

options.text: Marasmus -- lacking all food (total calorie deficiency)
Kwashiorkor -- lacking sufficient protein despite adequate calorie intake
Rickets -- lacking vitamin D
Anaemia -- lacking iron

questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is caused by severe protein deficiency, often while total calorie intake is adequate (typically from starchy foods like maize). The swollen belly is caused by fluid retention (oedema) due to low levels of blood proteins like albumin, which normally help regulate fluid balance by osmosis. The flaky skin and wasted muscles are also characteristic symptoms.

questions.stem: A patient is diagnosed with iron-deficiency anaemia. They feel constantly tired and short of breath. How does iron deficiency cause these symptoms?

options.text: Iron is needed for nerve function; without it, signals slow down
Iron is a key component of haemoglobin; less haemoglobin means less oxygen is carried to cells, reducing aerobic respiration
Iron deficiency causes the heart to stop beating
Iron is needed for digestion; without it, food is not absorbed

questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that binds and carries oxygen. With less haemoglobin, the blood carries less oxygen to the tissues. Cells cannot respire aerobically as efficiently, producing less energy (ATP). This causes tiredness, weakness, and shortness of breath as the body tries to compensate.

questions.stem: Rickets causes soft, bowed bones in children. It can be prevented by ensuring adequate intake of vitamin D and calcium. A doctor advises a child with early signs of rickets to spend more time outdoors. Why?

options.text: Fresh air contains calcium that can be absorbed through the skin
Sunlight on the skin stimulates vitamin D production, which helps the body absorb calcium for bone development
Exercise outdoors directly strengthens bones
Outdoor plants release vitamin D into the air

questions.explanation: The skin produces vitamin D when exposed to ultraviolet (UV) light from the sun. Vitamin D is essential for the absorption of calcium from food in the intestine. Without adequate vitamin D, calcium cannot be properly absorbed, and bones do not mineralise correctly, leading to soft, weak bones (rickets in children, osteomalacia in adults).

questions.stem: A student says 'deficiency diseases only affect people in developing countries.' Why is this statement incorrect?

options.text: Deficiency diseases have been completely eradicated worldwide
People in developed countries can also develop deficiency diseases due to poor diet choices, medical conditions affecting absorption, or restricted diets
Developing countries have the best nutrition in the world
Only genetic diseases affect people in developed countries

questions.explanation: Deficiency diseases can affect anyone with an inadequate diet, regardless of where they live. In developed countries, people on very restricted diets, those with eating disorders, elderly people with poor nutrition, or those with conditions like coeliac disease that impair absorption can all develop deficiency diseases. Iron-deficiency anaemia, for example, is common worldwide.
